summary: Saudi Arabia's restoration commitments comprise ongoing and planned afforestation, land restoration and rehabilitation initiatives covering approximately 4,000,000 hectares to combat desertification—about 2.1% of the country's total land area—in a 2022 landscape that is 93.9% bare area. The Kingdom also joins a collective G20 ambition to reduce degraded land by 50% by 2040. Its mixed restoration-and-conservation agenda targets a 30% enhancement of Red Sea coastal biodiversity by 2040 through coral-reef, mangrove, seagrass and native-vegetation restoration and rewilding, alongside an integrated aquifer-recharge system to capture and treat stormwater over 100 hectares by 2040. Conservation commitments seek protected marine areas covering 30% of coastal marine zones and preservation of 95% of nature within NEOM. The supplied land-cover data do not provide denominators for the coastal, degraded-land or NEOM percentages.

targets.metric: Afforestation, land restoration and rehabilitation area
